Editorial standard

When a chapter is ready

A chapter is published for study only after its evidence, teaching, and presentation pass review.

Source selection

Survey a broad, relevant set of accessible university courses. Record what was actually reviewed, not just what was found. Study the pertinent written material from at least four distinct courses at four universities, compare their explanations and proofs, and select the combination that best covers this chapter. Use more sources when a documented gap calls for them.

Lesson structure

  1. Identify chapter boundaries, prerequisites, and the exact sources used.
  2. Teach definitions and semantics before advanced transformations.
  3. Derive laws, state proof assumptions, and include countermodels and boundary cases.
  4. Provide five to ten demanding, fully worked original problems.
  5. Close with a concise review sheet of key ideas and later timed-problem pitfalls.
  6. List precise references and the limits of source review.

Length follows the material. Repetition and decorative pages do not improve coverage.

Quality gate

Check mathematical claims, formula transformations, problem answers, source attribution, links, and desktop, mobile, and print layout. Record any unresolved issue. A chapter with an identified content error or uncovered in-scope topic remains a draft. No finite review can guarantee a literal 100% success rate on unseen future questions; the editorial goal is to remove every identified error and gap.

Deferred exam practice

Archived Iranian master's and doctoral entrance-exam booklets are set aside until the final month. At that stage, we will work through their questions together, one by one, and use the results to diagnose and correct weaknesses. The first reading does not require the student to answer test questions.
